trigger_detail: Changed files cross API route/middleware, error-surface, config/settings and user-input-handling boundaries (backend/src/api/middleware.py reflects a caller-supplied X-Request-ID into logs and a response header; backend/src/config/logging.py owns PII redaction; backend/src/api/errors.py and backend/src/api/platform/routes.py are the public error and health surface).

instances.headline: VULN-001 high CWE-770 unbounded X-Request-ID reflected into log sink and response header; 8 MB header accepted, ~15.6 MB/s log amplification from a single unauthenticated client
0 BLOCK / 7 WARN; refuted CRLF, header-injection, JSON-log-injection and stack-trace-leak candidates by raw-socket test; rated unbounded header and inert redaction as WARN not BLOCK
VULN-001 high PII reaches log sink in cleartext via the exception path (RedactionFilter never touches exc_info/exc_text); VULN-002 high unbounded X-Request-ID

security.dissent_note: Instance 2 agreed on the same underlying facts (unbounded header, inert redaction, case/format-sensitive matching) but rated them WARN because it could not trace an attacker-controlled path to a money-accepting endpoint that does not exist yet. Instances 1 and 3 blocked on demonstrated impact against the live server. The disagreement is severity calibration, not contradictory evidence.

instances.headline: QA-VM-003 FAIL (2 of 4 in-window log lines parse as JSON); E15-S1-AC2 also FAIL — PII redaction bypassed at the uvicorn sink in the running server
QA-VM-003 FAIL (1 of 2 lines, 50%, deterministic over 3 trials); PII in query string leaks through the same bypassed access line
QA-VM-003 FAIL (50%, attributed by client port over a raw socket across 3 requests); unit test structurally blind because log_capture attaches to root and uvicorn.access does not propagate

functional.agreement_note: Unanimous, with independently derived root cause: uvicorn and uvicorn.access keep propagate=False plus their own DefaultFormatter/AccessFormatter, so their records never reach the root JSONLogFormatter that configure_logging installs. QA-VM-004 was passed by all three on its narrower 'request-scoped' wording; QA-VM-005 passed by all three well inside the 1 s budget.

code_review.note: Single instance by design — the 3-instance rule covers the security and functional axes only.

consensus_blocks: QA-VM-003 / E15-S1-AC3: not 100% JSON log lines while serving (3/3 evaluators, plus code-review CR-004)
PII redaction is inert in production: redact_values has zero production call sites, and the filter never scrubs exc_info/exc_text (evaluators 1-3, security 1-3, code-review CR-005/CR-016)
Unbounded X-Request-ID reflected into log sink and response header (security 1 and 3 BLOCK, security 2 WARN, evaluator 1, code-review CR-011)
unanimously_refuted: CRLF / HTTP response-header injection via X-Request-ID — h11 returns 400 for bare CR/LF/NUL/control bytes; a real CRLF split parses as two headers so the app sees only the prefix
JSON log injection / log forgery — json.dumps escapes the payload; the line stays one valid JSON object with a single request_id key
Stack-trace or secret leakage in error responses — app.debug is False, unhandled errors return a generic 500
XSS in MoneyText.tsx — JSX text interpolation, no raw-HTML sink
project-manifest.json duplicate 'mode' key — the file parses and verification.mode appears exactly once
regression-suite-full BLOCK — misapplied check: features.json has zero passes:true in any group, so group A is the first landed group and the prior-contract regression set is empty
